title: The Lean Office Advantage
author: Artur Henriques
summary: Henriques argues that commercial real estate is one of the largest unoptimized operational expenses on most companies' balance sheets, even as executive boards mandate three-to-four-day return-to-office policies while simultaneously chasing small efficiency gains from AI. He attributes the office-mandate push to a combination of a tighter job market, a management bias toward believing collaboration and performance assessment require physical presence, and sunk-cost pressure from multi-year commercial leases that make empty office space feel wasteful. His central proposal is a 'hot seat' hybrid model — employees in the office roughly two days per week — which he estimates could reduce required office space by around 60 percent and facilities costs (rent, supplies, cleaning, energy) by up to 50 percent, framing leaner office footprints as both a direct cost saving and a talent-recruitment advantage over competitors still requiring three to four days on-site.
points: The claim that commercial real estate is 'the single largest unoptimized operational expense' identifies a cost lever leadership discussions often overlook in favor of headcount or AI efficiency debates.

The observation that underperforming employees face 'the same challenges' in-office as remote — undercutting the core justification for RTO mandates — directly rebuts the productivity-assessment rationale companies commonly cite for requiring in-person work.

Naming sunk-cost fallacy and status-quo bias as drivers of RTO mandates (multi-year lease commitments making empty space feel wasteful) reframes office mandates as a rationalization of a prior financial commitment rather than a productivity-driven decision.

The specific quantified proposal — a 'hot seat' two-day-per-week model cutting required office space by around 60% — turns a general remote-work argument into an actionable real estate and staffing recommendation for leaders evaluating lease renewals.
quotes: Commercial real estate is the single largest unoptimized operational expense on in companies balance sheet.
While tech leaders fight to squeeze 5% efficiency gains out of AI strategies, executive boards are bleeding money by keeping office space to hold all the teams together at the same time.
However, even in an office context, and underperformed employee will have the same challenges as in a remote context. This might be the strongest bias against remote working.
It would not be far-fetched to target a 50% cost reduction on facilities expenses just by adopting a more flexible work model.

Even if a company would like to maintain an office, the amount of space required can be substantially reduced if it adopts a "hot seat" approach to hybrid work. By requesting that employees come to the office only 2 days per week, it can potentially decrease office space by around 60%.

If the market standard is having people in the office around 3-4 days per week, a company that pushes for around 2 days (or punctual visits) will have a higher chance of recruiting the best talent, all while maintaining a leaner cost structure.
